text:
maria: Heads up — prod is seeing intermittent DNS failures to external hosts (payments, s3). ~10% of requests time out or return SERVFAIL. Rolling users notice higher latency. Anyone seeing this in metrics?

kevin: yup saw increased DNS latency on the pod-level metrics. Graphs show CoreDNS latency spikes around 11:07 and 11:18 UTC. K8s events look normal.

aj: I checked CoreDNS pods, some logs: 
```
2026-01-19T11:07:18Z coredns[57]: 10.244.3.12:53421 - [11/Jan/2026:11:07:18 +0000] "A IN payments.internal.example.com. udp 60 false 512" SERVFAIL qr,rd,ra 123 0.001503ms
2026-01-19T11:07:18Z forward: error from 172.31.0.10:53: dial udp 172.31.0.10:53: i/o timeout
```

lucy: Noticed a pattern: failures only hit pods in eu-west clusters that egress through the new NAT gateway we deployed yesterday. us-west clusters stable.

maria: Good catch. NAT was swapped to the scalable gateway for eu-west yesterday at 10:30 UTC. Could be a change in source IP behavior or fragmented UDP responses.

aj: I did a quick tcpdump on one node when it failed. Observed DNS responses coming back from the upstream resolver IP but with a different source port than original query (so our node-local stub cache dropped them). Snippet: 
```
22:11:07.123456 IP 10.244.3.12.37412 > 172.31.0.10.53: 12345+ A? payments.internal.example.com.
22:11:07.123456 IP 172.31.0.10.53 > 10.244.3.12.56000: 12345 1/0/0 A 10.5.1.2
```
note the response used port 56000 not 37412.

kevin: That explains SERVFAIL for the node-local cache. Some NAT devices rewrite source ports for scalability. Our node-local-dns / kube-proxy expectation is reply port==query port. If NAT changes that we need TCP fallback or enable 'force-tcp' in CoreDNS forward?

lucy: Also we saw systemd-resolved on nodes earlier holding DNS in a stub resolver mode (127.0.0.53) which can mask the real port mapping. Combined with glibc's UDP-only stub, fragmented UDP answers and EDNS0 could make the client drop responses.

maria: Short-term mitigations? Suggestions: 1) enable TCP for CoreDNS <-> upstream for eu-west (increase latency but avoids port mapping issues) 2) roll back NAT gateway to previous implementation 3) reduce EDNS0/UDP size by setting 'max_udp_size' in CoreDNS or disable EDNS.

aj: I'm partial to config change first: set forward . { up ... } with policy random and add 'max_concurrent 20' and 'tls' or 'tcp' as fallback. Also can set 'bind' to 0.0.0.0 to avoid systemd-resolved weirdness. I'll create a canary deployment for one node pool.

kevin: I'll open a ticket with infra to check the NAT gateway port preservation settings and whether it supports 1:1 port mapping or only endpoint independent mapping. If it is endpoint-independent mapping we will see rewritten source ports.

lucy: Also worth reducing TTL on our internal records so cached negative responses don't linger. Some customers hit stale cached NXDOMAINs. Dob: set lower negative-ttl in CoreDNS.

maria: Action items:
- aj: canary CoreDNS config change to prefer TCP for upstream and reduce EDNS size (start now).
- kevin: infra ticket to NAT vendor + rollback plan if needed.
- lucy: adjust negative TTLs and add a health check that queries both UDP and TCP.

sre-bot: Incident created: S-2026-013 — 'eu-west DNS intermittent SERVFAIL due to NAT port rewrite' assigned to #infra oncall. Priority P2.

aj: Canary applied to nodepool eu-west-canary at 11:33 UTC. Early results: clear reduction in SERVFAILs from 9.8% -> 0.9% for that pool.

maria: Great. Keep monitoring. If canary stays green for 30m we can roll. Also we should document this NAT port-rewrite caveat in the runbook (resolv.conf, node-local-dns, CoreDNS adjustments).

kevin: Filing postmortem stub: we should add a test that simulates NAT port remap and verifies node-local-dns behavior in CI. I'll link the NAT vendor config in the ticket.

lucy: FYI vendor said their new scalable NAT uses endpoint-independent mapping for performance. They have an alternate mode with port-preservation but it doesn't scale. We'll need to choose tradeoffs.

maria: Thanks all. Rolling to full eu-west with TCP fallback in 30m unless objections. :thumbsup:
